Jeg vil gå litt off topic här, håper det er ok 🤗

Er det noen som bruker norsk bank för att ta ut FIAT til som ikke er så hostile?
messages.translation:
I'm going to go a bit off topic here, hope that's ok 🤗

Is anyone using a Norwegian bank for cashing out to FIAT that isn't so hostile?

messages.text: Har du mer informasjon om saken din?
messages.translation: Do you have more information about your case?

messages.text:
Jag har egentlig bare cashat ut en gang. Tidlig desember 2021. 

Sparebank1 låste kontot mitt under kanskje tre uker, men jag var i kontakt med en boliglånshandlegger under den tiden så han hjelpte meg før å få kontot åpnet igjen. Ett knappt år etterpå fick jeg dokk en varning når jeg overförte litt penger till Kraken att de ikke ville vara delaktiga i kryptovalutaoverføringer.

DNB litt värre. Låste kontot mitt utan att gi meg beskjed. Kom som en overraskning når jeg skulle bruke kortet mitt i vardagen. Mitt konto i DNB var sannsynligvis under oppsikt og blokkert efter 500.000 nok i transfereringer. Ingen att henvende meg til. Kundeservise opplyser meg om att den avdelingen ikke går att kontakta. 

Det tog nok sirka to månader att låsa opp kontot etter att ha startet den lange formelle klageveien som skulle kommit att involvera banktillsynet.

Jeg har en følelse att det ikke kommer å bli lettare under høsten 2025 når neste uttag vil skje. Hørt mye gott om Revolut, men det er ju en utenlandsk bank og hvis jeg vill bruke NOK  her i Norge så er jeg urolig att samma problem vil oppstå :(
messages.translation:
I've actually only cashed out once. Early December 2021.

Sparebank1 locked my account for maybe three weeks, but I was in touch with a mortgage advisor during that time, so he helped me get the account opened again. Barely a year later I did get a warning when I transferred some money to Kraken, saying they didn't want to be involved in cryptocurrency transfers.

DNB a bit worse. Locked my account without telling me. Came as a surprise when I was going to use my card in everyday life. My DNB account was probably under surveillance and blocked after 500,000 NOK in transfers. No one to turn to. Customer service informs me that that department can't be contacted.

It took about two months to get the account unlocked after starting the long formal complaint process that was going to end up involving the financial supervisory authority.

I have a feeling it's not going to get any easier in the autumn of 2025 when the next withdrawal will happen. Heard a lot of good things about Revolut, but it is a foreign bank, and if I want to use NOK here in Norway I'm worried the same problem will come up :(

summary.headline: A quiet Norwegian Nexa channel: troll bans, wallet and event news, and complaints about crypto-hostile banks.
summary.summary: This window stretches from April 2024 into 2026 in a very low-traffic group, so it reads as a series of short bursts rather than a continuous conversation. It opens with moderators jQrgen ⛛, Rose (bot), Bbob and Ede repeatedly banning a returning troll they identify as 'Hyper', whom Bbob explains is still bitter that cyber/allstar was never reinstated as community manager. After that, jQrgen ⛛ and endo mostly post project news: the Wally Nexa iPhone wallet beta and its App Store launch, the KnowNexa video series, the ScriptQuest developer challenge with a $6k prize pool, AusCryptoCon sponsorship, and the successful first Nexa mainnet hard fork in March 2025. The longest substantive discussion comes from roastbacitracin, a Swede living in Norway, who details how Sparebank1 and DNB froze his accounts after crypto cash-outs and how it took months and a formal complaint to resolve. Between these, there is friendly small talk, greetings, event chatter (Nordic Blockchain Conference, a discounted BTC halving festival ticket, a possible Oslo hackathon meetup) and a brief question about whether the Blitz FPGA card can mine, which jQrgen ⛛ answers with a flat no.

topics.title: Banning a persistent troll
topics.summary: jQrgen ⛛ used /dban repeatedly (with Rose the bot confirming), while Bbob and Ede discussed the serial account-maker 'Hyper', whose grievance Bbob traced back to cyber/allstar not returning as community manager; jQrgen ⛛'s remarks grew increasingly scathing.

topics.title: Norwegian banks hostile to crypto
topics.summary: roastbacitracin asked which Norwegian bank is least hostile for cashing out to fiat and then gave a detailed account of Sparebank1 freezing his account for three weeks and DNB blocking it without notice after 500,000 NOK in transfers, taking two months and a formal complaint to unlock; jQrgen ⛛ asked follow-ups and suggested Revolut supports NOK.

topics.title: Wally wallet and Nexa announcements
topics.summary: jQrgen ⛛ shared the TestFlight beta and later the App Store release of the Wally Nexa Wallet for iPhone; endo and Onur_Chinaski posted official items including KnowNexa episode 4 on Tailstorm, the ScriptQuest NexScript developer challenge with $3k/$2k/$1k prizes, and the successful first mainnet hard fork at block 766,084.

topics.title: Events and meetups
topics.summary: jQrgen ⛛ floated an Oslo gathering around a future hackathon, offered a half-price ticket to the Bitcoin halving festival he could no longer attend, and asked who was going to the Nordic Blockchain Conference; Ede said she would check her schedule, and jQrgen ⛛ noted a Norwegian contingent was attending.

topics.title: Newcomers and small talk
topics.summary: roastbacitracin joked about lacking Norwegian citizenship after 20 years in Norway, confirmed jQrgen ⛛'s Bitcoin Unlimited membership, and the group traded morning greetings; Ede translated endo's quip that Norwegian is hard to learn.

topics.title: Blitz FPGA card question
topics.summary: roastbacitracin relayed a question about who benefits from the Blitz card and whether it earns mining rewards; jQrgen ⛛ first didn't recognise the name, then confirmed Blitz is not for mining.

topics.title: Liberstad legal status
topics.summary: jQrgen ⛛ quoted material noting Liberstad has no concessions from the Norwegian government and is still legally Norway, wondering aloud what the exit plan is.

summary.mood_description: The window starts with irritation and some mockery as moderators clear out a repeat troll, with jQrgen ⛛ and Bbob openly contemptuous of someone they see as wasting his energy on anonymous complaining. After that the tone settles into a sparse, easygoing rhythm of greetings, event invitations and official Nexa news, with genuine enthusiasm around the Wally iPhone wallet release and the hard fork. The one clearly sour note later on is roastbacitracin's frustration with Sparebank1 and DNB freezing his accounts, which the group treats sympathetically rather than dramatically. Overall the channel feels small and collegial rather than energetic.

highlights.why: Bbob's backstory on the recurring troll explains the grudge behind the repeated ban waves.
The window's most substantive post: a detailed first-hand account of Norwegian banks freezing accounts over crypto cash-outs.
Concrete product milestone - the Wally Nexa wallet going live on the iOS App Store.
Official ScriptQuest developer challenge with a $6,000 prize pool and deadline details.
Announcement that Nexa's first mainnet hard fork activated successfully, with an upgrade requirement for full node operators.
